title: Calibration: dominant-strategy truthfulness in second-price versus first-price auctions
question: Does the research loop reproduce two known results about sealed-bid auctions, and does it refute a hypothesis that is known to be false? Setting: two bidders, values and opponent draws uniform on [0, 1]; second-price opponent bids x, first-price opponent bids x/2 (the equilibrium strategy).

hypotheses.statement: In a second-price auction, bidding one's value is weakly dominant: no deviation on the bid grid ever beats truthful bidding on any sampled opponent bid.
hypotheses.falsifier: At least one sample in which some grid bid earns more than the truthful bid by more than 1e-12.

hypotheses.statement: In a first-price auction against an opponent bidding x/2, bidding v/2 earns strictly more expected utility than bidding v, for every tested value v.
hypotheses.falsifier: For some tested v the 95% lower bound of the gain (bid v/2 minus bid v) is not above zero.

hypotheses.statement: Negative control. In a first-price auction against an opponent bidding x/2, truthful bidding earns positive expected utility.
hypotheses.falsifier: The 95% upper bound of truthful expected utility is at or below zero for every tested value. It is known to be exactly zero, so this hypothesis is expected to be refuted.
